slowest_experiments.experiment: V621 Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight

summary: All 3 completed experiments were compute-bound within 18.4 minutes. Chat-correct three-family SOTA entrance bank was longest at 16.95 minutes; the supplied evidence has no phase data explaining why.
bottlenecks_identified: Chat-correct three-family SOTA entrance bank concentrated nearly all recorded wall time in one compute-bound experiment.
No phase-level timing was supplied for the longest experiment, so its duration cannot be attributed to loading, inference, scheduling, or teardown.
Task-aligned accelerator, concurrent-model-count, and runner-selection records were absent, preventing a supported GPU-efficiency assessment or determination of a DualGPURunner dispatch miss.
improvements_suggested: Add structured phase timers to the three-family entrance-bank workflow so the next critical path has a causal breakdown.
Record accelerator samples inside each experiment's start and end boundaries instead of relying on an uncorrelated monitor snapshot.
Emit a launch receipt with concurrent model count and runner choice, and automatically select DualGPURunner only when two or more models are explicitly loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add conditional launch planning that selects DualGPURunner for confirmed parallel multi-model workloads while retaining the single-GPU path for single-model inference.
Instrument the entrance-bank workflow with phase-level elapsed-time records.
Join GPU utilization samples and runner-selection receipts to experiment lifecycle identifiers.
meta_reflection: Fallback timing localized the critical path but did not expose its cause. A point-in-time GPU report cannot establish compute-window utilization, and no data available this milestone establishes that a parallel multi-model task missed DualGPURunner; without a measured alternative, estimated savings remain unquantified.
